drip-irrigation-process.title: Drip Irrigation — End‑to‑End Design & Operation
drip-irrigation-process.discription: Comprehensive guide covering principles, components, hydraulic design, scheduling, fertigation, maintenance, troubleshooting, and a bill of materials template for drip irrigation.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Drip irrigation delivers water at a controlled, low discharge directly to the root zone using emitters distributed along laterals. The objective is to match soil intake capacity and crop demand while minimizing evaporation, runoff, and deep percolation.

A complete system typically includes: water source and pumping, filtration, pressure regulation, main and sub‑main conveyance, laterals with emitters, valves and automation, fertigation, and flushing points.
bullets: Typical operating pressure at emitters: 0.7–1.5 bar (10–22 psi).
Common emitter discharges: 1, 2, 4, 8 LPH (liters per hour).
Uniformity depends on pressure stability, filtration efficiency, and hydraulic design.

steps.title: Controlled application
steps.details: Emitters convert inlet pressure into a small, steady flow (drops or tiny streams). Water infiltrates around the dripper, forming a wetted bulb that overlaps with neighboring bulbs when spacing is correct.

steps.title: Filtration first
steps.details: Screen, sand/media, or disc filters remove suspended solids and bio‑load that would otherwise clog emitters. Filtration is sized to water quality and emitter orifice.

steps.title: Stable pressure
steps.details: Pressure regulators and balanced pipe sizing keep pressure variation low across the block so each emitter delivers near its rated discharge.

steps.title: Periodic flushing
steps.details: Ends of mains and laterals include flush valves or removable end caps to purge sediment and biofilm at startup and after fertigation.

items.name: Water source & pump
items.function: Provide adequate flow and head. Include foot valve/strainer when drawing from open sources.
items.sizingNotes: Pump head must cover filter loss, regulator loss, pipe/friction loss, elevation, and minimum emitter pressure.

items.name: Filtration unit
items.sizingNotes: Use sand/media filter for high organic load, screen or disc for fine particles; size to system flow with backwash capability.

items.name: Fertilizer injection (venturi or dosing pump)
items.function: Inject soluble fertilizers into irrigation water.
items.sizingNotes: Provide non‑return valves and a bypass; place after filters to avoid media contamination.

items.name: Main & sub‑main pipes
items.function: Convey water to field blocks with minimal head loss.
items.sizingNotes: Keep velocity 0.6–1.5 m/s; add air‑release valves at high points; provide flush points at ends.

items.name: Laterals
items.function: Carry water to emitters along crop rows.
items.sizingNotes: Limit lateral length based on diameter, emitter spacing, and allowable pressure variation (usually ≤20%).

items.name: Emitters / drippers
items.function: Meter flow to the root zone.
items.sizingNotes: Choose discharge (LPH) per crop/soil; pressure‑compensating types help on slopes or with varied lengths.

items.name: Valves & automation
items.function: On/off control, zone selection, automatic scheduling.
items.sizingNotes: Combine manual/solenoid valves with timers/controllers; add pressure gauges across filters.

details: Map field dimensions, slopes, and elevation differences.
Locate water source, electricity, and maintenance access.
Identify soil texture (sand/loam/clay) and infiltration rate.
Document row spacing and plant spacing; estimate canopy spread.
Decide laterals per row (vegetables: 1–2; orchards: emitters or ring layout).
Set emitter spacing by root zone and soil spread.
Target application rate at or below soil intake rate.
Divide farm into hydraulic blocks so total flow fits pump capacity and filter rating.
Keep lateral lengths uniform within a block.
Select main/sub‑main diameters to keep friction losses reasonable.
Confirm velocity 0.6–1.5 m/s to avoid sediment settlement or water hammer.
Add isolation valves per block and pressure gauges for monitoring.

sections.title: Hydraulic calculations
sections.notes: Keep pressure at the most downstream emitter ≥ the minimum rated value. Sum all head losses and elevation changes.

formulae.name: Hazen–Williams head loss (SI)
formulae.variables: L: length (m), Q: flow (L/s), C: HW coefficient (PVC ≈ 150), d: internal diameter (m)
formulae.note: Convert to pressure with 1 bar ≈ 10 m head.

formulae.name: Allowable pressure variation along a lateral
formulae.note: Use ≤10% for high‑value crops or very long laterals.

workedExample.title: Quick lateral check
calc: Flow per lateral = 120 × 4 LPH = 480 LPH = 0.133 L/s
Estimate friction using Hazen–Williams (C=150) and verify ΔP < 0.2 bar
If ΔP is high, shorten lateral or increase diameter.
workedExample.result: Choose lateral length/diameter to meet ΔP constraint; then size sub‑mains for balanced block pressure.

patterns.name: Vegetable beds (drip tape)
patterns.description: Parallel laterals along each bed; 20–30 cm emitter spacing; tape 12–16 mm.

patterns.name: Orchards (point source)
patterns.description: 2–4 emitters per tree; expand to ring as canopy grows.

patterns.name: Vineyards (in‑line PC)
patterns.description: Pressure‑compensating inline laterals on sloping blocks.

sections.title: Irrigation scheduling
sections.summary: Schedule by crop water requirement (ETc), soil water holding capacity, and system application rate.
method: Compute reference evapotranspiration (ETo) from local weather or station data.
Select crop coefficient (Kc) by stage; ETc = ETo × Kc.
Application time per event = Net depth / Application rate × Field efficiency.
sections.applicationRateNote: Keep emitter application rate below soil intake to prevent ponding—sands accept higher rates than clays.
sensors: Use tensiometers or capacitance probes to trigger irrigation at thresholds.
Mulch reduces evaporation; adjust runtime downward when mulched.

sections.title: Fertigation
why: Delivers nutrients to the active root zone with high efficiency.
Allows split applications timed to growth stages.
procedure: Backflush filters; inject through the manifold after filtration.
Start with clean water, begin injection at target ppm, finish with clean water rinse.
Monitor EC and pH; avoid precipitation (e.g., calcium with phosphates).
safety: Store acids/fertilizers separately; use PPE during mixing.

sections.title: Maintenance & flushing
checklist: Daily: read inlet/outlet pressure across filters; backwash when differential exceeds the threshold.
Weekly: open lateral end caps and flush until water runs clear.
Monthly: chemical treatment (chlorination/acid) if biofilm or scale is observed.
Seasonal: inspect emitters, repair rodent/mechanical damage, replace worn tape.

fixes: Increase pipe diameter or shorten laterals
Adjust fertigation chemistry; inject acids if scale forms
Ensure adequate NPSH; adjust pump/water level

terms.def: Liters per hour — common dripper discharge rating.
Pressure‑compensating emitter that maintains constant flow across a range of inlet pressures.
Evenness of water distribution; influenced by pressure variation and clogging.
Reversing flow through a filter to remove trapped particles.

items.q: How long can a 16 mm lateral be?
items.a: Depends on emitter spacing/flow and allowable pressure variation; many designs keep laterals within 60–100 m. Shorten on steep slopes or use PC emitters.

items.q: Do I need both sand and screen filters?
items.a: If the source has organics or algae, include a sand/media filter followed by screen/disc for fine particle protection.

items.q: What’s a good starting pressure at emitters?
items.a: Many emitters perform well at around 1.0 bar; check your model’s rating and keep variation low across the block.

diagram.title: System flow (text schematic)
lines: Water Source → Pump → Sand Filter → Screen/Disc Filter → Pressure Regulator → Main Line
Main Line → Sub‑Mains → Valves → Laterals → Emitters → Root Zone
Bypass: Fertilizer Injector (after filters) → Back to Main
Flushing: End caps/flush valves at mains and laterals
